summary: Alabama's State Building Code (2021 International Building Code and 2021 International Plumbing Code) covers state-funded buildings, schools, hotels, motels and movie theaters, and uses the 2010 ADA Standards for accessibility. Other commercial restrooms follow the building and plumbing codes their city or county adopted.
quote: The requirements of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design supersede the accessibility requirements contained in the International Building Code and ANSI A117.1.

summary: Arizona has no statewide building or plumbing code; each city or county adopts its own, mostly editions of the International Codes. Arizona's own disability law applies the 2010 ADA Standards to public accommodations and commercial facilities.

to_confirm: The building and plumbing code editions adopted by the city or county (some Arizona cities use the Uniform Plumbing Code, others the International Plumbing Code; not checked per city). R10-3-404 was read on Cornell LII (amended effective February 7, 2012), not on an Arizona state site.

summary: California uses its own statewide codes: the 2025 California Building Code, whose Chapter 11B sets accessibility rules for commercial restrooms, and the 2025 California Plumbing Code, both in force since January 1, 2026. Cities and counties enforce them and may add stricter local amendments.

summary: The District applies the 2017 DC Construction Codes, which are the 2015 International Codes with District amendments, including the building and plumbing codes. Accessibility follows the 2009 edition of ICC A117.1 referenced by the building code.
quote: The 2017 DC Construction Codes consist of the 2015 International Code Council (ICC) family of model codes, the 2014 National Electrical Code, and 2013 ASHRAE 90.1, as amended by the District of Columbia Municipal Regulations (DCMR) Title 12, Sections A through M.
to_confirm: DOB took over code development in February 2026 and says it aims to adopt new construction codes by the end of 2027 (search result of DOB pages, not opened), so recheck the edition before each update. The DOB page naming each 2017 code and its model code (dob.dc.gov/page/2017-dc-construction-codes) returned HTTP 403; the plumbing edition rests on the 'family of model codes' sentence. The A117.1-2009 reference was read in the referenced-standards chapter of DOB's integrated 2017 Building Code PDF, which doesn't show amendments after May 29, 2020.

The 8th Edition (2023) applies now and the 9th Edition (2026) applies to permits applied for from December 31, 2026.
quote: The Effective Date for the Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023), is December 31, 2023.
to_confirm: The 9th Edition date (12/31/2026) was read in the Florida Building Commission's October 2026 workplan (https://www.floridabuilding.org/fbc/commission/FBC_1026/Commission/Workplan_October_2026.pdf); a City of Tampa notice reportedly says January 1, 2027, so confirm the changeover date with the local building department and update this entry once the 9th Edition is in force. No official page was read that names the Accessibility volume's edition in one sentence; it rests on the statute plus the Commission's 8th Edition course listings.
